sourceContractFindings.title: Closed fallback and nested field contracts are not fully declared
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: humanInputRequests is a required envelope field; Section18 lists eight control kinds and rejects unknown keys, but the complete source never enumerates its permitted nested keys, value types, requiredness, cardinalities, question/answer bindings or choice representation. FIELD_REGISTRY closure supplies static ownership/default classes, not a unique nested schema. TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION is likewise named without an expression/value grammar.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: A hand-authored closed schema could reject valid author interpretations or accept unsafe undeclared shapes. The source expressly says an ununiquely specified field contract is UNDEFINED_FIELD_CONTRACT.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Require an exact source-derived schema or narrowly scoped normative amendment. Reconciler must distinguish ordinary structure choices explicitly allowed by the source from release-bearing semantics that the closure rule forbids inventing.

sourceContractFindings.title: Stage17/19 per-run scope does not specify runId targets
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Stage17 and Stage19 include EXECUTE_RUN and VERIFY and require ten new independent run targets. TARGET_SLOT is derived from operation-specific identities required by Section14.7. That matrix omits runId for both stages; non-designated dimensions are prohibited unless registered immutable references, while run creation needs a reserved target. The family-reuse sentence does not expressly add scope dimensions.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: A literal matrix yields the same target slot for multiple run operations in one iteration; silently adding runId changes the closed scope contract. The problem is source-level, not a claim about existing implementation behavior.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Reconcile whether the family-reuse rule uniquely imports the Stage11/12 per-operation run scope. If not, specify the exact Stage17/19 per-operation scope, target classifications and target-slot preimages before accepting those operations.

sourceContractFindings.title: Stage19 independent requirement-discovery challenge lacks an explicit operation contract
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Stage19 completion expressly requires an independent requirement-discovery challenge. Its closed operation set is CONFIRM_FREEZE, EXECUTE_RUN, VERIFY, COMPARE, REGRESSION_VERIFY, CONFIRM. CONFIRM is application-owned. The source does not say which external operation produces that challenge, which canonical family owns it, its allowed context/material, trigger/universe, reviewer/reconciler route, or how new requirement candidates enter current authority. semanticChallenges declares Stages1,3,4, not19.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: The mandatory Stage19 completion predicate cannot be independently proven by a uniquely specified operation merely by inventing a challenge-complete boolean or adding an unlisted operation.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Identify a unique existing operation and full writable/input/independence contract through source reconciliation, or amend that narrow contract. Do not add an unapproved stage or Operation31.

sourceContractFindings.title: Named Test IR primitives do not fully specify release-bearing semantics
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: The source demands exact named input/output ports, types/cardinalities/error propagation and one compatible language identity, but provides a partial example and operation names rather than the complete operation signatures/semantics. Examples unresolved by the text include SORT comparison/type policy, UNIQUE equality, empty SUM/MIN/MAX behavior, REGEX output/flags, and every operation error-code map. Parser/dialect and numeric edges likewise need a unique normative contract. Section34.3 prohibits inventing release-bearing derivation semantics.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: Two reasonable implementations could accept different programs or compute different gate results while advertising the same closed-loop-test-ir-language/1 and operations/1 identities.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Reconcile the intended complete primitive/port/type/error/parser/numeric contracts against an explicitly named normative algorithm or obtain a narrow source contract. Explicit resource-limit constants remain an allowed implementation choice under21.14 and should not be confused with this gap.

sourceContractFindings.title: Expected-variance contracts have no complete frozen schema or evaluator
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: The current source requires Stage06 expected-variance contracts and Stage13 comparison under a frozen contract. expectedVarianceContracts lists ownership, normalized contract/hash/evaluation use; no closed dimension/value schema, allowed-versus-prohibited rule, required freezing event, comparison result derivation, or semantic adjudication acceptance is supplied. The only Stage13 reference says allowed variance recorded, prohibited variance defects, UNKNOWN blocked.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: Unexplained-variance zero and convergence could become implementation-chosen; all-ten agreement also lacks a fully stated formula for mixed statuses beyond the two example test cases.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Close the exact fields, freeze dependency, variance evaluation and semantic-review route. A reconciler may prove simple count derivations from source but must not generalize the examples into unstated release thresholds.

sourceContractFindings.title: Per-operation minimum input-binding basis is required but not assigned
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Section26.6 requires every external operation to declare MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS, offers four bases, and limits echoed identities to at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. It does not enumerate or provide a unique selection rule for each operation role. This contrasts with39.13 explicitly assigning SELF_ASSERTED identity assurance for all current human-decision purposes.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: The same file-first operation could be accepted or blocked solely by an implementation-selected evidence threshold. Byte-exact possession may never accept SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN, but that prohibition alone does not select a unique stronger threshold.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Derive exact role-specific minima from controlling clauses if possible; otherwise register a narrowly approved normative assignment, preserving observable versus provider-hidden limits.

sourceContractFindings.title: Raw-unitization version names a contract without complete deterministic media rules
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: closed-loop-raw-units/1 requires stable media-specific units, treatment of pages/sections/archives/embedded objects/comments/annotations/tracked changes/metadata and unsupported formats. The source supplies categories and mandatory trigger limits, but no complete segmentation/chunking/locator algorithm or supported-format boundary. Under34.3 release-bearing normalizers/derivations require specified semantics or named normative algorithm.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: Different unitizers can produce different denominators and challenge triggers under one version. A whole-file fallback for supported subdivision is expressly prohibited.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Confirm what algorithm is uniquely fixed versus delegated; if none, close the minimal raw-unitization contract without weakening thresholds or claiming arbitrary semantic enumeration.

sourceContractFindings.title: DUE_NOW deadline formula and first-available deferred-test case require reconciliation
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Section16.1 derives DUE_NOW only when stage is at or beyond REQUIRED_BY_STAGE in addition to earliest stage and availability. Section41 case178 says a deferred test becomes due at the first valid target stage, and32.4 requires target-aware timing. When target first exists before REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, literal rules may diverge.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: Premature blockers or omitted first-available execution may result depending on whether due means executable eligibility or deadline enforcement.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Specify executable-now versus due-for-gate semantics and the exact deferred-target rule; preserve future obligations without premature preproduct gating. Do not silently rewrite the deadline formula.

sourceContractFindings.title: Terminal disposition and delivery state must be distinguished explicitly
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Section1 applies REJECTED/BLOCKED/ACCEPTED precedence to every terminal determination. Section36.9 and Stage30 create an AUTHORIZED or BLOCKED delivery determination, otherwise BLOCKED when prerequisites are not all true. This may be consistent if controlling disposition and delivery state are distinct axes; their complete closed relationship is not explicit.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: A mandatory refutation must not be mislabeled as mere uncertainty, while no rejected/blocked terminal can authorize transfer.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Reconciler should first establish that distinct fields/axes are already entailed by the source; only if not, request minimal contract clarification. This is not a request to add REJECTED to the delivery-state enum arbitrarily.

sourceContractFindings.title: Expiration predicates need an exact time and lifecycle contract
sourceContractFindings.source_only_observation: Deletion receipts include retention expiry and physical challenges reject expired evidence, but the source does not prescribe their retention/expiry duration, triggering condition or governing clock. Delivery real-time validity explicitly cannot rely on device time.
sourceContractFindings.acceptance_impact: A selected implementation default could permit replay, lose exact retry guarantees or reject valid device evidence. Some expiry may legitimately be dependency-based rather than wall-time, so absence of a duration alone is not proof of conflict.
sourceContractFindings.required_reconciliation: Document a uniquely authorized expiry/retention rule and its evidence basis; determine whether governance may select this parameter or whether closed release-bearing derivation rules require a source amendment. Do not invent expiration facts.

exceptionsAndNonrequirements.rule: A substantive runtime requirement may independently resemble an implementation instruction; that does not authorize embedding the specification or management packet.

Physical dedup may share blobs; canonical occurrence/role artifacts remain distinct. Initially required files may be empty, included exact duplicates or human-excluded; inaccessible material cannot silently disappear.
Later exact-byte transfer is allowed when relevant representation needed; it is not semantic resupply. Unavoidable browser reselection after failed capture is permitted with exact prior identity.
Nonblocking human question must still be asked; explicit unknown/deferred answer can permit Stage01, researchable unknown must not be pushed to human.
Evidence-supported no-source is valid after actual bounded search/independent adequacy; source-count preference never limits controlling sources.
Fixed small launcher/copy convenience and diagnostic/accessibility text fallback may exist, but no canonical clipboard dependency or weaker validation.
Optional Stage27 advisory is non-gating and cannot delay/modify/substitute for release.

Exact newly confirmed human answer may co-commit dependent proposal atomically. Correction/inconsistency invalidates; existing human values not reconfirmed. Auto-commit is permitted only within closed narrow conditions.
Nondue future target obligations remain scheduled; do not count as satisfied, omit them, or require meaningless preproduct matrix cells.
Canonical handoff is logical files, not ZIP. Deterministic archive profile applies only app-produced archives; external inbound archive safety+slot extraction. Sequential exports suffice on iPhone.
OS duplicate-name transport suffix may be tolerated with independent exact binding; no delivery-artifact rename authorization follows.

Additional primitive or specialized adapter only when demonstrated necessary; unsupported schema/format semantics route externally. Complete third-party JSONPath/XPath/general JSON Schema support is not automatically required.
Explicit centralized resource constants are selected by implementation, documented and boundary-tested; this is an express design discretion, unlike undefined release-bearing semantics.
Generally routable human/independent review at Stage06 does not prove later execution or external/provider independence. Application-established means only observable dimensions.
Read-only or demonstrably safe reversible action may use normal authority; all other specified risk classes need genuine bound decision, UNKNOWN blocks.
Blind alias is inappropriate when true identity is tested or would undermine proposition; do not hide necessary identity.
Genuine authorized scope change or authoritative waiver changes governing proposition/version; it never converts existing violation into SATISFIED. Severity cannot excuse mandatory refutation.
Empty universe can pass only independently reviewed, evidence-supported and current; optional metrics cannot invent convergence thresholds.
Legitimate regression retirement requires all safeguards; expense, flakiness, difficulty or failure do not justify it.
Host Unicode can be used only after pinned conformance fixtures; otherwise bundled tables. Ordinary array order preserved unless explicitly registered set.
In-origin package is not external backup, hash self-consistency not authentication; credentials require encrypted backup profile. No unsupported stronger evidence claim.
Failed run attempts are replaceable in the same target slot with a fresh context; accepted run is not rerun in same iteration and failed contexts never count toward ten.
Own commit and unrelated operational status events do not self-stale dependency-bound derived proof; later affecting changes do. Terminal-only registry finding need not mutate Stage27.
SELF_ASSERTED operator assurance is explicitly sufficient for every current decision purpose; do not add authentication as an invented blocker.
Exactly one mechanically identifiable approved predecessor can be proposed baseline; ambiguous/unestablished approval needs actual human baseline decision.
Exact hardware model and WebKit build may UNKNOWN; minimum tuple required. Recorded human physical observation is sufficient and must never be rebranded app proof.
Historical wording create runtime/increment /3 means implement target if missing, not rewrite conforming code or invent /4.
Same real project may satisfy maturity conditions if actually evidenced; synthetic fixtures or empty meaningless objective cannot replace real outcome.
Embedded historical hashes/commits/report are historical leads, not current acceptance.

Closed-Loop Reliability Application
Zero-Loss Controlling Implementation Specification

Specification status: Controlling implementation and acceptance specification
Repository: sjonesjones917/closed-loop-tracker
Normative specification path: specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt
Specification manifest path: specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json
Normative requirement manifest path: specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json
Canonical deployment origin: https://sjonesjones917.github.io
Canonical deployment base path: /closed-loop-tracker/
Workflow identity: mobile-closed-loop/30
Required stage count: Exactly 30
Target project schema: closed-loop-project/3
Target response schema: closed-loop-stage-response/3
Test IR schema: closed-loop-test-spec/1
Verification-package schema: closed-loop-verification-package/1
Contract profile: closed-loop-completion-profile/1
Subject model: Project-subject neutral
Execution model: Application-native deterministic execution wherever the proposition can be faithfully represented; otherwise exact routing to an independent AI reviewer, capable external tool, human inspection, or external system
Primary objective: Maximize the probability that the final delivered product is actually correct while preventing unsupported confidence and minimizing opportunities for human or AI error.
0. Controlling execution instruction
This is an implementation task, not an audit, discussion, architecture exercise, or request for a downloadable patch.

The implementation agent MUST:
1. Inspect the actual repository and establish the true current starting commit.
2. Modify the existing application directly.
3. Preserve every working mechanism that satisfies this specification.
4. Correct every repository behavior that conflicts with this specification.
5. Implement the smallest complete changes necessary.
6. Test the application through the visible live user interface as a human operator would use it.
7. Exercise the workflow in order.
8. Test every affected downstream path after every upstream correction.
9. Preserve every reproduced defect as a permanent regression.
10. Deploy the corrected application.
11. Verify the exact deployed bytes.
12. Use the deployed application through the real operator path before claiming completion.

The implementation agent MUST NOT:
1. Return an audit as a substitute for implementation.
2. Return a patch archive, downloadable bundle, replacement project, or instructions for the user to install manually as a substitute for modifying the actual application.
3. Stop after editing only Stage 01, Stage 04, or another isolated portion.
4. Declare success because source code looks correct.
5. Declare success because syntax tests pass.
6. Declare success because unit tests pass.
7. Declare success because deployment succeeds.
8. Declare success before replaying the exact failed user path in the live application.
9. Change unrelated visuals.
10. Perform cleanup, refactoring, renaming, architecture modernization, or style changes that are not required to correct a demonstrated defect.
11. Rewrite working systems merely because another design is possible.
12. Create parallel stores, engines, parsers, prompt systems, shells, or workflow implementations.
13. Ask the user to repeat information the application already possesses.
14. Make the user manually allocate identifiers, calculate hashes, construct schemas, connect routine relationships, calculate gates, or retype canonical information.
15. Place instructions intended for external agents anywhere except the exact generated prompts controlled by prompt-engine.js.
Automated tests are mandatory, but they are not a substitute for live operator-path verification. Both are required.

The controlling repair discipline is:
One observable failure → identify the earliest responsible layer → apply one minimal complete correction → replay the exact visible path → verify affected downstream behavior → preserve the failure as a regression.
0.1 Implementation-instruction boundary

Section 0 directs only the implementation agent modifying and verifying the repository. Its instructions are not runtime project requirements, external-stage instructions, canonical project data, operator content, or prompt content. The application MUST NOT copy, paraphrase, display, store, export, or delegate Section 0 or other user-to-implementation-agent instructions into project records, operator screens, generated prompts, execution packages, schemas, or delivered artifacts unless a separate substantive product requirement expressly requires the same runtime behavior. prompt-engine.js contains only instructions needed by the external actor for the current project stage and operation.
1. Controlling acceptance disposition
The controlling disposition for every gate, stage determination, release determination, and terminal determination is evaluated in this exact order:
1.1 Any current sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition -> REJECTED.
1.2 Otherwise any required unknown, insufficiency, contradiction, stale state, unresolved blocker, or unavailable mandatory capability -> BLOCKED.
1.3 Otherwise every applicable mandatory proposition satisfied -> ACCEPTED.
1.4 All blockers and contradictions remain recorded even when REJECTED controls the disposition.

Additional controlling principles:
- The authoritative external prompt is a file, not clipboard contents or a rendered preview.
- The authoritative external response is an ingested JSON file, not pasted text.
- A human-origin answer stated only to an external agent remains an agent report until the application records human confirmation.
- A stage obligation is not due before its defined target exists and its EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached.
- Authorization to deliver is not evidence that delivery occurred.
- Implementation instructions are not runtime agent instructions.
2. Normative source and governance manifests
2.1 Normative-source and runtime boundary

The controlling normative source is the exact UTF-8 file `specification/closed-loop-reliability-controlling-implementation-specification.txt` in the exact audited source commit. CI MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-specification-manifest.json` as a repository-only closed-loop-specification-manifest/1 after reading those exact bytes and MUST generate `specification/closed-loop-normative-requirements.json` as the corresponding normative-requirement manifest. That manifest records the source commit, repository path, artifact filename, byte length, SHA-256, section inventory, contract-profile identity, and the identity and digest of the normative-requirement manifest. The manifest and source commit together identify the exact specification used for implementation and acceptance; the specification does not contain a self-referential digest of itself.

The controlling runtime contract profile is closed-loop-completion-profile/1. Runtime project state, prompts, responses, packages, imports, exports, and receipts carry only the contract profile and the particular schema or registry identities required for their own operation. The specification text, its repository-only manifest, Section 0 implementation instructions, user-to-implementation-agent instructions, audits, and repair commentary are not runtime project data and MUST NOT be embedded in the application, generated prompts, execution packages, canonical records, or operator screens merely to establish conformance.

A closed-loop-project/3 object that lacks the current contract profile is legacy /3 data. It MUST be deterministically migrated with complete migration receipts or preserved as historical and non-gating. Schema-name equality alone does not establish current contract conformance.
2.2 Normative-requirement manifest

Repository governance MUST maintain one machine-readable closed-loop-normative-requirements/1 manifest generated from and reviewed against the controlling specification. It assigns a stable NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT_ID to every distinct normative requirement, prohibition, invariant, field contract, operation contract, negative case, regression obligation, deployment obligation, and definition-of-done metric. Each entry records the controlling text location, responsible implementation owner, schema or registry entry, deterministic and semantic test IDs, mutation-test IDs, required browser or physical-device proof, acceptance-report field, and current disposition.

This manifest is implementation and acceptance evidence outside runtime project state. It MUST NOT be injected into ordinary project prompts or carried by the application as project content. CI rejects missing, duplicated, untraced, or conflicting normative entries and rejects an acceptance claim when any current mandatory entry lacks the required implementation and proof relationships.

Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. CI records the challenge and reconciliation evidence with the manifest digest. An unreconciled material disagreement, an uncovered section, or a missing challenge record blocks acceptance.
3. File-first and iPhone operating outcome

For every external-agent operation, the application exports the exact authoritative prompt as a UTF-8 text file and exports any required manifest and input artifacts as files. The external agent returns one authoritative UTF-8 JSON response file plus any declared returned artifacts. The application ingests those file bytes directly. Clipboard copy, pasted JSON, and large text-entry transport are optional nonauthoritative conveniences only and cannot be required for completion.
The required physical mobile operator path is the pinned actual-iPhone Safari acceptance target defined in Section 45. Browser-neutral desktop verification remains required where specified.
4. What the application may and may not guarantee
4.1 Required deterministic guarantees

Permitted fail-closed dispositions include:
- REJECTED
- BLOCKED
- UNDETERMINED
- EXECUTION_FAILED
- HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED
4.2 Prohibited false guarantees

Preferred reliability language is:
100% conformant to the tested deterministic invariants, with measured operational reliability of X.
For zero observed silent failures across N materially independent accepted operations, the approximate 95% upper bound 3/N may be reported.
4.3 Additional deterministic guarantees
5. Product lifecycle
The controlling lifecycle has two valid commit paths.

External semantic or production work:
human authority
→ raw intake and file custody
→ application reservation
→ exact prompt-file and handoff-package generation
→ external conversation or execution
→ authoritative response JSON file and returned-file selection
→ exact raw-byte staging
→ parse and validation
→ proposal
→ human acceptance only where the mutation contract requires human acceptance
→ canonical commit
→ deterministic derivation
→ stage gate
→ exact next action

Application-owned work:
validated application command
→ deterministic execution or derivation
→ atomic application-owned commit
→ stage gate
→ exact next action

Final delivery:
product eligibility
→ delivery-candidate freeze and inspection
→ exact artifact identity verification
→ evidence-chain closure
→ atomic terminal determination
→ authorized export or share action
→ delivery-attempt evidence at its actual epistemic basis
No application-owned calculation is converted into a human-approved semantic proposal merely to fit a single lifecycle pattern.
6. Exact Stage 01 information flow
This section resolves the central Stage 01 implementation failure.
6.1 Before Stage 01
Before Stage 01, the application possesses only raw human input and files the user has supplied.

Store-once refers to physical byte storage: identical bytes may share one stored blob. Canonical artifact identity is per supplied occurrence and role — the same bytes supplied again, or under a different filename or role, remain distinct ARTIFACT_ID records referencing shared storage. Deduplication never merges canonical artifact records.

The application MUST NOT pretend it semantically understands arbitrary file contents before an agent or supported deterministic parser has inspected them.
There is no hidden pre-Stage-01 semantic intake agent.
6.2 The Stage 01 agent is the first semantic reader
Stage 01 is the first semantic extraction stage.
The Stage 01 agent MUST NOT assume that another agent extracted the file previously.
6.3 File transfer into the Stage 01 agent context
Files stored in browser-local application storage are not automatically present in an external AI conversation.
The user may have to perform a transfer action because external contexts cannot access browser-local bytes automatically.
The application must use the already stored bytes.
6.3A Authoritative Stage 01 handoff

The application MUST generate the Stage 01 prompt as the authoritative prompt file defined in Section 10.1 and a manifest-bound file set containing every required raw input artifact. The operator attaches or shares those exact files to the external agent. The application MUST NOT require the operator to copy the prompt, paste file bodies, reconstruct a package, or reselect source bytes that the application already stores.
6.4 One-time semantic intake
After the Stage 01 agent has inspected the request and supplied files, the accepted semantic intake becomes reusable canonical project information.
The application MUST NOT require the user to attach the intent file repeatedly merely so later agents can rediscover the same facts.

A later independent context may still require transfer of actual bytes when the exact file representation is itself necessary. In that case, the application MUST prepare the stored file or the smallest exact package automatically. That is a file-transfer operation, not a request for the user to resupply the information.
6.4A External-conversation human-answer capture

The external agent may ask concise human-authority questions in the external conversation. A human-origin answer first supplied there remains an EXTERNAL_CLAIM until the agent returns it in the response JSON and the application presents the exact extracted answer for one-action confirmation or correction. The resulting confirmation creates the HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION record and provenance link. Exact confirmation may be atomically co-accepted with the dependent proposal under Section 14.10; correction requires a replacement prompt. The operator is not required to retype the answer. Facts already present in current raw input or accepted human records are not reconfirmed.
6.5 Stage 01 coverage accounting
The Stage 01 accounting model MUST have two distinct layers.
The application MUST NOT falsely claim to have semantically enumerated arbitrary file statements before the Stage 01 agent reads them.

The application MUST require the Stage 01 response to account for every application-provided raw input unit using one of these dispositions:
- EXTRACTED_RELEVANT_INFORMATION
- RETAINED_AS_CONTEXT
- NO_PROJECT_RELEVANT_INFORMATION
- UNRESOLVED_HUMAN_AUTHORITY
- LATER_RESOLVABLE
- INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED
Every extracted statement MUST link to one or more raw input units and exact source locations where available.

Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.
6.5A Raw-unitization contract

Raw-input accounting MUST use one versioned RAW_UNITIZATION_VERSION — current value closed-loop-raw-units/1 — with deterministic media-specific unit rules. Text-message boundaries, structured text units, document pages and sections where mechanically available, archive members, embedded documents, native images and media, unsupported-format whole-file fallbacks, and source locations receive stable application-owned unit identities.

The unitization contract explicitly defines treatment of comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata, embedded objects, inaccessible content, and unsupported formats. A supported subdivision cannot be replaced by one whole-file unit merely to make coverage vacuous. SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1 triggers a challenge when any one of these thresholds is exceeded: 1,048,576 stored bytes in one text or document artifact; 100 mechanically countable pages; 20 supplied files or archive members; 500 raw units; or 5,242,880 aggregate supplied bytes. A material uncovered unit, broad exclusion, INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED material, material uncertainty, contradiction, or operator request triggers regardless of size. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.
6.6 Mandatory two-pass Stage 01 procedure
The Stage 01 prompt MUST require:

Pass 1 — exhaustive extraction
Read the complete request and every accessible supplied artifact from beginning to end. Extract all distinct project-relevant human-origin statements.
The agent MUST resolve identified omissions before returning final JSON.
Raw coverage plus this mandatory semantic process provides enforceable accounting without falsely representing arbitrary semantic understanding as a deterministic application calculation.
7. Stage 01 purpose, boundaries, and questions
7.1 Purpose
Stage 01 is complete human-authority intake.
7.2 Required extraction
7.3 Question classes
Every unresolved issue belongs to exactly one category:

BLOCKING_NOW
- The answer must come from the human.
- The answer is required to define the Stage 01 job or deliverable.
- Stage 01 cannot complete until it is answered.

ASK_NOW_NONBLOCKING
- The answer must ultimately come from the human.
- It is foreseeable and should be asked during Stage 01.
- The human may answer "unknown" or "deferred."
- Stage 01 may complete after that explicit answer.

LATER_RESOLVABLE
- The matter can be resolved from supplied materials, authorized research, or a later stage.
- The agent must not ask the human merely because the answer is not yet known.
- The item is retained with its later resolution path.

The controlling logic is:
- Must come from human → ask now.
- Human says unknown or deferred → preserve that answer.
- Can be established from available material or authorized research → do not ask the human.
- Needed to define Stage 01 and unanswered → HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED.
- Needed only later and the human already had an opportunity to answer → Stage 01 may proceed with a tracked unresolved item.
"Nonblocking" never means "skip the question."
7.4 Human conversation
Questions MUST be presented as normal concise conversation.
One strict final JSON response file is returned only when Stage 01 is ready for ingestion.
7.4A Human-authority provenance

An external agent may propose that a statement originated with the human, but it cannot create or modify a HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION value. A newly reported human answer becomes authoritative only through the application confirmation path in Section 14.10. Confirmation presents the extracted answer and permits accept or correct without retyping. The application records the exact external response pointer, confirmed value, human decision receipt, and resulting input version.
7.5 Subject neutrality
prompt-engine.js MUST NOT contain runtime branches for patent, legal, medical, software, AEC, mechanical, CAD, CAM, CNC, scientific, financial, or other project subjects.
A patent fixture may test whether the generic algorithm elicits relevant human-only issues. That fixture MUST NOT become a patent-specific production branch.
7.6 Stage 01 completion

Stage 01 MUST NOT force the operator to review a reconstructed line-by-line copy of everything already supplied.
Human confirmation is limited to genuine human-authority decisions.
8. Stage 02 and Stage 03 boundaries
8.1 Stage 02
Stage 02 inventories independent external sources that may govern, inform, or prove correctness.
A user-supplied project artifact is not automatically an independent external authority.

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. UNKNOWN blocks wherever the item could be mandatory. A source-mandated or nonwaivable obligation cannot be weakened by an agent or unsupported human exception.

A controlled exception never converts a violated proposition into SATISFIED. It is either an authorized scope change creating new input and requirements versions, an authoritative waiver represented as a new governing obligation with its own proposition and evidence, or a blocker where authority is insufficient. Sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition blocks release regardless of severity. UNKNOWN severity blocks severity-dependent routing.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NFC normalization and default case folding use Unicode 15.1.0 data. Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. Every set-valued array has one named versioned normalizer. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. No implementation selects preimage fields implicitly.

For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. 35.6 Reservation and idempotency state machine

If the transaction begins at project revision R, it commits reservationRevision = R + 1. The package expectedRevision and the response scope projectRevision are exactly reservationRevision. Acceptance requires the current project revision to equal reservationRevision except for an exact idempotent retry already covered by the receipt.

Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

Resuming an ORPHANED reservation verifies the same binding and changes no identity. A new authoritative reservation for the slot is prohibited until the old reservation is terminal. An exact idempotent retry returns the original receipt even when the project has advanced to the command's committed revision. A different normalized payload under the same key is rejected.
35.7 Deletion and clone idempotency receipts

The metadata store retains minimal nonproject command receipts necessary for idempotent DELETE_PROJECT and CLONE retries. A deletion tombstone contains only deleted JOB_ID, commandId, idempotency key, normalized payload hash, deletion result, committed metadata sequence, and retention expiry; it contains no substantive deleted project content. An exact retry returns the prior result.

A clone receipt is stored outside both source and clone project bodies and binds source project/hash, clone command identity, payload hash, resulting clone JOB_ID, mapping-manifest identity, and result. An exact retry returns the same clone rather than creating another. Conflicting retries are rejected.

Each state records its actual evidence and epistemic basis. A package generated or duplicated inside the same IndexedDB origin is not an external backup; browser-local duplicate data in the same origin is not disaster-recovery backup evidence. Production maturity requires a successful restore from the exact exported package bytes.

closed-loop-encrypted-export/1 uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit cryptographically random IV per encrypted payload, a fresh 128-bit random salt, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations to derive the 256-bit key from the operator passphrase, and the canonical unencrypted package manifest digest as authenticated additional data. The container records algorithm, KDF, iterations, salt, IV, ciphertext length, and authentication tag. The passphrase and derived key are never persisted. IV reuse under one key is prohibited. Authentication failure rejects the export or restore without partial activation. CREDENTIAL_SECRET backup material requires this encrypted profile and cannot use an acknowledgment-only unencrypted export.

Before the terminal Stage 30 calculation, the application creates a PRE_DELIVERY_CHECKPOINT bound to the exact Stage 27 through Stage 30 prerequisite records and every authorized artifact byte identity. The checkpoint is exported under the backup policy and its CHECKPOINT_ID is a terminal prerequisite and delivery-record field. Project metadata never points to PENDING bytes. 41. Mandatory deterministic and behavioral tests

Execution routing
1. Registered native test → no external action.
2. Unsupported native test → blocked.
3. External-agent test with capability and bytes → executable.
4. External-agent test with missing capability → blocked.
5. External-agent test with missing bytes → blocked.
6. Human inspection → human action.
7. Independent review → independent-review action.
8. External system → external-system action.
9. UNAVAILABLE → blocked.
10. Metadata-only artifact cannot satisfy a byte requirement.
11. Verified artifact can satisfy byte readiness.
12. Artifact later loses verified availability → readiness revoked.

Independence
13. Ten unique run contexts → potentially established.
14. Duplicate context across two runs → violation.
15. Generator and verifier share context → violation.
16. Distinct verifier context → potentially acceptable.
17. Agent claims independence but context identities prove reuse → violation.
18. Different IDs with explicit contamination → violation.
19. Same candidate across all ten → batch identity passes.
20. One different candidate → batch integrity fails.
21. Prior-run output in authorized inputs → contamination.
22. Reviewer feedback in run inputs → contamination.

Evidence sufficiency
23. Byte test with prose only → insufficient.
24. Byte test with verified hashes and identities → sufficient.
25. Meaning test with hash only → insufficient.
26. Meaning test with product location, observed meaning, comparison, and applicable source evidence → sufficient.
27. Human inspection with agent assertion only → insufficient.
28. Human inspection with human-owned evidence → sufficient.
29. External-system test without attributable system evidence → insufficient.
